label: Comma/quote/dash boundary (or the first letter of 'i.e.', 'т.е.', 'd.h.', 'c'est-à-dire') right where the text is about to restate or gloss the preceding term ('i.e.', 'that is', 'то есть', 'أي'); strongest in Russian, Arabic, German and French prose. Output promotes ' i', ' namely', '即', 'cioè'.

probed_before.source: this checkout's .probe-log, before the pre-registration commit

notes: 10x pilot (concept-maps/tenx, random arm): label and 16 sentences written by a fresh Sonnet 5.5 subagent from a packet (card + all-pole band samples); no probes. An Opus gate checked rule-level items only (8 + 8, 0 overlap with census and probe text, near misses free of the declared trigger) and edited nothing. Labeller's note: Top examples are all the token right before an appositive gloss (i.e./т.е./d.h./c'est-à-dire), with output promoting ' i', ' namely', 'cioè'; the neuron is very sparse (0.009% above 0.3 max) and bands show it also fires weakly on many bare commas, so near misses use commas that lead to ordinary continuations. The - pole (commas before 'which means/that is' definitions) looks related but opposite in sign, and fire items may land under 0.3 of max since the max (400) is an outlier.
